summary: A 1932 CCC-built steel tower in the NJ Pine Barrens, replacing an earlier tower moved to Stokes State Forest; still actively staffed today.

facts.design: McKlintock-Marshall 86-ft steel tower with 7'x7' metal cab (CCC, 1932)

events.note: First tower at the site reported erected and opened by the state's 1920-21 annual report (an Aermotor model, per NHLR)

NHLR's Blue Anchor page says the original Aermotor tower was removed and re-erected at Stokes State Forest as the Culver tower; NHLR's own page for that lookout (Culvers Lookout, US44/NJ1) instead dates its present 47-ft Aermotor tower to 1933 and does not mention Blue Anchor, so the identification and the exact year are unconfirmed
Current 86-ft McKlintock-Marshall steel tower with 7x7-ft cab built by the CCC, replacing the relocated tower
Added to the National Historic Lookout Register, March 15, 2004, nominated by Bob Spear

notes_for_editor: Good corroboration across a historical register, a period newspaper quote (Courier-Post, 1940), the Wikipedia tower-list table, and a 2024 news feature confirming the tower is still actively staffed; all of those checked out against their cited sources. One claim did not hold up on cross-check: NHLR's Blue Anchor page says the original Aermotor tower was relocated to Stokes State Forest in 1932 to become 'the Culver tower,' but NHLR's own page for that lookout (Culvers Lookout, US44/NJ1) dates its present 47-ft Aermotor tower to 1933 and never mentions Blue Anchor — so the 'same tower, still standing at Stokes' claim in the earlier draft was an overclaim, now softened and the discrepancy disclosed in the story. Also removed an invented 'winter of 1920-21' detail not supported by the cited annual-report quote. No source found on public climbing access, so access.level was left unchanged rather than guessed.
